title: The Room That Wasn't There
script: Guest: [frustrated] I booked this room three months ago and paid in full. How exactly does a hotel run out of rooms that were already reserved?
Receptionist: [apologetic] I completely understand your frustration, and I'm sorry this has happened. Occasionally more rooms are reserved than we actually have available.
Guest: [incredulous] That sounds like a problem you created, not one I should be expected to solve at eleven at night.
Receptionist: [calm] You're right, and it isn't your responsibility. What I can offer is a suite at a partner hotel two streets away, at no extra cost.
Guest: [wary] A suite sounds like compensation dressed up as generosity. What's actually included, and how do I get there at this hour?
Receptionist: [reassuring] Breakfast, late checkout, and a taxi, all arranged and paid for by us. I can have the driver waiting within ten minutes.
Guest: [softening] That's more reasonable than I expected, though I'd still like something for tomorrow, given the inconvenience tonight.
Receptionist: [accommodating] Understandably so. I can credit one night's stay back onto your original reservation once you return here tomorrow.
Guest: [considering] Provided the room tomorrow is actually available, unlike tonight's, I suppose that works.
Receptionist: [honest] I've personally confirmed it this time, rather than relying on the system, precisely because I don't want a repeat of this.
Guest: [wry] I appreciate the honesty. It's more than most people offer when something's gone wrong on their end.
Receptionist: [warmly] For what it's worth, this isn't how we like guests to be treated, and I've flagged it for the manager already.
Guest: [relenting] Alright. I'll take the taxi and the suite, and we'll call it resolved, provided tomorrow goes smoothly.
Receptionist: [grateful] Thank you for your patience. I'll text you the confirmation and the driver's details right away.
Guest: [half-joking] Just make sure the suite actually exists, unlike this room apparently didn't.
Receptionist: [smiling] I promise it does. I checked myself, twice, after tonight's mix-up.
Guest: [warming] Good. I'd rather trust you than the booking system, honestly.
Receptionist: [warmly] A wise choice tonight. Safe trip across town, and I'll see you tomorrow.

quiz.question: What problem does the guest discover at check-in?
options: His card was declined
The hotel has no room for him despite his reservation
He booked the wrong dates
The hotel is under renovation
quiz.explanation: Despite booking and paying three months in advance, the hotel has run out of available rooms, a case of overbooking.

quiz.question: Why does the receptionist say the overbooking happened?
options: A computer virus deleted bookings
Occasionally more rooms are reserved than the hotel actually has available
The guest arrived too late
Another guest refused to leave
quiz.explanation: She explains that occasionally more rooms end up reserved than the hotel actually has available.

quiz.question: What does the receptionist offer as a solution for tonight?
options: A refund only
A suite at a partner hotel with breakfast, late checkout, and a paid taxi
A discount voucher for next time
A room to share with another guest
quiz.explanation: She offers a suite at a nearby partner hotel, with breakfast, late checkout, and a taxi all arranged and paid for.

quiz.question: What does the receptionist do differently to reassure the guest about tomorrow's room?
options: She upgrades him permanently
She personally confirmed the room herself, rather than relying on the system
She calls the manager to apologise
She offers a full refund instead
quiz.explanation: She says she personally confirmed tomorrow's room herself, rather than relying on the system, to avoid a repeat of the problem.

quiz.question: How does the guest's attitude change by the end of the conversation?
options: He remains angry and demands a refund
He softens and agrees to the arrangement, trusting the receptionist over the booking system
He cancels his stay entirely
He asks to speak to the manager
quiz.explanation: By the end, the guest relents, accepting the arrangement and saying he'd rather trust her than the booking system.
